questions.question: Parents are being prepared to take home an infant who is fed through a jejunostomy tube. Which point should the nurse stress in the discharge teaching?
options: Administer high-calorie formula orally to promote weight gain
Monitor the jejunostomy site daily for signs of infection or leakage
Clean the jejunostomy tube with alcohol-based solution twice daily
Restrict fluid intake to prevent excessive output from the jejunostomy
questions.explanation: Daily inspection of the exit site is the cornerstone of home care. Parents are taught to look for redness, swelling, warmth, discharge, excoriated skin, granulation tissue and leakage of feed around the tube, to keep the site clean and dry, to check the external marking so displacement is recognised, and to report any of these promptly. Leaking jejunal contents rapidly erode the surrounding skin, and a dislodged tube is an emergency because the tract closes quickly.

explanations.A: A jejunostomy is placed precisely because the oral or gastric route is unsafe or inadequate. Nutrition goes through the tube, usually as a continuous or slow intermittent infusion since the jejunum cannot handle bolus volumes; any oral intake is introduced only on the team's advice.
explanations.B: Daily inspection of the exit site is the cornerstone of home care. Parents are taught to look for redness, swelling, warmth, discharge, excoriated skin, granulation tissue and leakage of feed around the tube, to keep the site clean and dry, to check the external marking so displacement is recognised, and to report any of these promptly. Leaking jejunal contents rapidly erode the surrounding skin, and a dislodged tube is an emergency because the tract closes quickly.
explanations.C: Alcohol dehydrates and irritates peristomal skin and can degrade the tube material. Mild soap and water, dried well, is the recommended routine.
explanations.D: Withholding fluid in an infant on jejunal feeding invites dehydration and electrolyte disturbance. High output is managed by adjusting the rate, concentration or formula composition, and by replacing losses, not by limiting what the child receives.

questions.question: The parents of a 5-year-old with asthma are being taught about a metered-dose inhaler of Asthalin (salbutamol), 2 puffs to be taken every 6 hours. Which instruction matters most?

Use a spacer device for effective delivery
Increase to 4 puffs if symptoms worsen
Administer before meals only
questions.explanation: A young child cannot reliably coordinate actuation with a slow deep inhalation and cannot hold the breath for ten seconds. A valved holding chamber removes the need for that timing, lets the child breathe tidally through it for five to six breaths, cuts the high-velocity oropharyngeal impaction and roughly doubles the drug reaching the lower airway. Below 5 years the spacer is fitted with a face mask; above that a mouthpiece is used, and rinsing the mouth afterwards is still advised.

explanations.A: The drug has been prescribed on a fixed six-hourly schedule, so restricting it to attacks contradicts the order. Salbutamol can be used both as scheduled relief and as rescue medication.
explanations.B: A young child cannot reliably coordinate actuation with a slow deep inhalation and cannot hold the breath for ten seconds. A valved holding chamber removes the need for that timing, lets the child breathe tidally through it for five to six breaths, cuts the high-velocity oropharyngeal impaction and roughly doubles the drug reaching the lower airway. Below 5 years the spacer is fitted with a face mask; above that a mouthpiece is used, and rinsing the mouth afterwards is still advised.
explanations.C: Doubling the dose on the family's own initiative masks deteriorating control and delays medical review; excess beta-2 stimulation also brings tremor, tachycardia and hypokalaemia. Escalation belongs in a written action plan agreed with the clinician.
explanations.D: Inhaled salbutamol acts locally on airway smooth muscle and its absorption is not influenced by food, so linking doses to mealtimes serves no purpose.

questions.question: Among the drugs used in the standard first-line regimen for tuberculosis, which one is considered to have the greatest bactericidal power against the tubercle bacillus?

Ethambutol
Isoniazid
Pyrazinamide
questions.explanation: Rifampicin blocks DNA-dependent RNA polymerase and kills bacilli wherever they sit, whether multiplying briskly in cavities, lying semi-dormant in caseous foci or hiding inside macrophages. This breadth of killing, plus its powerful sterilising effect that permits short-course therapy, is why it is ranked the most bactericidal of the first-line drugs.

explanations.A: Rifampicin blocks DNA-dependent RNA polymerase and kills bacilli wherever they sit, whether multiplying briskly in cavities, lying semi-dormant in caseous foci or hiding inside macrophages. This breadth of killing, plus its powerful sterilising effect that permits short-course therapy, is why it is ranked the most bactericidal of the first-line drugs.
explanations.B: Ethambutol inhibits arabinosyl transferase and is essentially bacteriostatic at usual doses. It is added mainly to protect the companion drugs against emerging resistance.
explanations.C: Isoniazid is strongly cidal against rapidly dividing extracellular bacilli and in fact shows the highest early bactericidal activity in the first two days of treatment, but its reach into slow-growing and intracellular populations is narrower than that of rifampicin.
explanations.D: Pyrazinamide comes into its own only in the acidic environment inside macrophages and inflamed lesions, killing the persisters that shorten therapy. Outside that niche it is largely inactive, so it is not the most bactericidal drug overall.

questions.question: Oxygen at 50 percent concentration is running at high flow for a 4-year-old. How should the delivered gas best be humidified?
options: Use a dry oxygen delivery system
Provide intermittent humidification with a heated humidifier
Administer saline nebulization every hour
Use a cold mist humidifier continuously
questions.explanation: A heated humidifier is the appropriate device whenever flows are high or oxygen is given for more than a short period. Warming the water to near body temperature allows the gas to carry far more water vapour than a cold bubble system can, so it arrives at close to body temperature and full saturation, keeping the mucosa intact and secretions mobile. Water temperature and level are checked, condensate is drained away from the child, and the circuit is changed per unit policy to limit bacterial growth.

explanations.A: Piped oxygen is anhydrous. Delivered dry at high flow it strips moisture from the airway lining, thickens secretions, paralyses ciliary clearance and causes nasal pain, epistaxis and mucus plugging — a particular hazard in the narrow airways of a small child.
explanations.B: A heated humidifier is the appropriate device whenever flows are high or oxygen is given for more than a short period. Warming the water to near body temperature allows the gas to carry far more water vapour than a cold bubble system can, so it arrives at close to body temperature and full saturation, keeping the mucosa intact and secretions mobile. Water temperature and level are checked, condensate is drained away from the child, and the circuit is changed per unit policy to limit bacterial growth.
explanations.C: Hourly saline nebulisation is not a humidification strategy. It delivers repeated fluid boluses to the airway, may trigger bronchospasm and interrupts the continuity of oxygen delivery.
explanations.D: A cold or bubble humidifier adds relatively little water vapour because cool gas holds less moisture, so it is inadequate for high-flow oxygen; cold aerosol can also provoke bronchospasm in a child with irritable airways.

questions.question: Light-headedness and one episode of almost blacking out bring a 65-year-old man to the emergency department. He has had diabetes mellitus for years and is known to have coronary artery disease. His monitor shows a slow rhythm made up of broad QRS complexes. options: Amiodarone
Transcutaneous pacemaker insertion
Anticoagulant therapy with continuous observation
Atropine
questions.explanation: A bradycardia that is producing symptoms of poor perfusion, such as near-syncope, and that carries a wide QRS suggesting block below the AV node, is an indication to capture the heart electrically. Transcutaneous pacing restores an adequate rate immediately while definitive therapy is arranged.

explanations.A: Amiodarone belongs to the tachyarrhythmia toolkit. Given to a patient who is already too slow, it depresses conduction further and can push the rate down towards asystole.
explanations.B: A bradycardia that is producing symptoms of poor perfusion, such as near-syncope, and that carries a wide QRS suggesting block below the AV node, is an indication to capture the heart electrically. Transcutaneous pacing restores an adequate rate immediately while definitive therapy is arranged.
explanations.C: Anticoagulation lowers clot risk but does nothing about a failing conduction system, and simply watching a patient who is already fainting allows the rhythm to deteriorate before help is given.
explanations.D: Atropine is the opening drug in symptomatic bradycardia, yet its vagolytic action works at the AV node. In high-grade, infranodal block with wide complexes it usually fails, so the algorithm moves on to pacing.

questions.question: A breathless patient has arterial blood gases reported as pH 7.50, PaCO2 28 mmHg and HCO3 24 mEq/L. Which condition best explains this pattern?

explanations.C: Air embolism can also cause sudden hyperventilation, but it is uncommon and requires a specific event such as central line manipulation or a neurosurgical procedure. Pulmonary embolism remains the far more probable explanation.

questions.question: Failure of the outflow foramina of the fourth ventricle, namely the foramina of Luschka and Magendie, to open normally is the underlying defect in which of the following conditions?
options: Dandy Walker malformation
Arnold Chiari malformation
Hydrocephalus due to aqueductal stenosis
Spina bifida
questions.explanation: Atresia of the lateral and median apertures traps cerebrospinal fluid inside the fourth ventricle, which balloons into a posterior fossa cyst. The associated hypoplasia or agenesis of the cerebellar vermis, with an enlarged posterior fossa and raised tentorium, completes the Dandy-Walker picture.

explanations.A: Atresia of the lateral and median apertures traps cerebrospinal fluid inside the fourth ventricle, which balloons into a posterior fossa cyst. The associated hypoplasia or agenesis of the cerebellar vermis, with an enlarged posterior fossa and raised tentorium, completes the Dandy-Walker picture.
explanations.B: In Chiari malformation the cerebellar tonsils and part of the medulla are displaced downwards through the foramen magnum; the apertures themselves are formed, and hydrocephalus arises from crowding at the craniovertebral junction.
explanations.C: Aqueductal stenosis narrows the cerebral aqueduct linking the third and fourth ventricles, so the fourth ventricle stays small while the ones above it dilate, exactly the reverse of the Dandy-Walker pattern.
explanations.D: Spina bifida is a defect of posterior neural tube closure over the spine. It may accompany a Chiari II malformation, but it is not a disorder of fourth-ventricular outflow.

explanations.A: The channel joining the pulmonary artery to the descending aorta is the ductus arteriosus, which closes after birth to become the ligamentum arteriosum.
explanations.B: The ductus venosus carries well-oxygenated blood from the umbilical vein straight into the inferior vena cava, bypassing the hepatic sinusoids so that the most oxygen-rich blood reaches the heart and brain. It closes after birth and persists as the ligamentum venosum.
explanations.C: The umbilical arteries carry deoxygenated blood away from the fetus to the placenta; it is the umbilical vein, not the artery, that relates to the portal system, and the ductus venosus is the shunt that bypasses it.
